notes: Identity checked independently from document contents: title The Red-Anger Effect: Is it Nothing More Than Demand Characteristics? and authors Daniel Wolf, Lukas Röseler, Johannes Leder, Astrid Schütz match the reference; header DOI 10.31234/osf.io/ntukz matches. Full 40-page primary manuscript with methods, results, discussion and references, not an abstract-only excerpt or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Both assigned inputs give identical Study 2, perceived-anger and p.25 locators without design/condition or critical contrast; neither identifies which of the two design-specific effects it targets. Do not map these tests to audit IDs by input order. Candidate presence-of-demand unpaired comparison: d = -0.43, t(220) = -3.22, p = .001; paired alternative dz = -0.44, t(110) = -4.59, p < .001. Candidate absence-of-demand comparison: d = 0.20, t(216) = 1.46, p = .145. Page 25 also reports facial-coloration main effect F(1, 436) = 2.54, p = .112, partial eta squared = 0.01 and coloration-by-design interaction F(1, 436) = 11.63, p < .001, partial eta squared = 0.03. No conversion performed. Candidate participant N: presence-of-demand n = 111; absence-of-demand 104 + 114 = 218, summing explicitly mutually exclusive final default-only and red-only groups (p.21). Overall final Study 2 N = 329 (p.19) is not selected as a contrast-specific analytic N. The unpaired presence comparison treats the repeated ratings as unpaired; 111 is unique participants, not independent recruited groups or a df-derived N. Exclusions: 160 of 489 recruited participants excluded, including 160 noncomputer users and 2 under 18 overlapping those exclusions; no missing-value exclusions (pp.18–19). Original side and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
